props.title: From Beginning to End
props.initialSlug: A bond forged in flesh and blood.

sections.content: From Beginning to End tackles the controversial subject of incestuous love through the story of two Brazilian half-brothers, marking director Aluizio Abranches's bold exploration of taboo relationships. The film shares thematic DNA with other boundary-pushing Brazilian cinema like Central Station (1998) and City of God (2002), though it ventures into more provocative territory. The intimate portrayal of Francisco and Thomas's relationship challenges viewers while maintaining a surprisingly tender, non-exploitative approach that echoes the sensitive handling of complex relationships in Y Tu Mamá También (2001).

sections.content: Brazilian cinema of the 2000s pushed boundaries in depicting complex family dynamics and sexuality. Madame Satã (2002) explored marginalized identities in Brazilian society, while Love Strange Love (1982) caused controversy with its taboo relationships. From Beginning to End fits into this tradition but takes an unusually gentle approach to its provocative subject matter, focusing on emotional intimacy rather than shock value. SUBHEAD: Breaking Taboos in World Cinema

The film's handling of forbidden love connects to a broader tradition of transgressive cinema, from Catherine Breillat's Fat Girl (2001) to Park Chan-wook's Oldboy (2003). However, Abranches eschews the typical shock tactics of these films, instead drawing influence from the tender approach of Happy Together (1997) and Brokeback Mountain (2005) in depicting love society deems unacceptable.
